subject: Design and Technology
weekly_outcome_verbatim: FOODWISE: prepare a 2-3 step dish safely.
scope: Week 2 only. Supervised preparation of the actual Week 1 planned dish. Food Weeks 1 to 3, then textiles Weeks 4 to 6. No later lesson is included.

accepted_predecessor.basis: Owner acceptance and local bytes independently verified.

model_dish: Cold bean and vegetable wrap with fruit and plain yoghurt
method: After the adult’s checks, wash hands with soap and water and dry them. Wash the carrot, cabbage and apple. Grate the carrot and finely slice the cabbage with adult-approved tools and supervision. Use prepared vegetables if agreed.
Mash 80 g of cooked beans labelled ready to eat with a fork. Mix in about 20 g from the single 60 g yoghurt portion. Add the carrot and cabbage. An adult opens tins and removes sharp lids.
Put the filling on the wholemeal wrap and fold it. Serve with the apple and the remaining yoghurt. Ask the adult to check the plate and store or serve it safely. Tasting is optional.
portion_note: These are the Week 1 model quantities for one person. Use the pupil’s actual approved plan and any checked substitution. Individual needs and appetite vary. One 60 g yoghurt portion is split: about 20 g in the filling and 40 g alongside.
adult_gate: Before ingredients are issued, use the school allergy policy and individual healthcare/access records, complete the blank teacher note privately, check every actual label and substitution, and confirm trained supervision, emergency arrangements, handwashing, safe tools, clean preparation and chilled storage. Unknown or incomplete checks mean HOLD. Do not infer no allergies from a blank record.
allergy_note: Thirteen response fields are wholly blank in both masters. Teacher completes privately from current school records and actual label checks. Unknown information means HOLD. No pupil details or example allergies are filled in.
evidence: Actual dish and plate record, observed preparation and safety actions, exact adult support, real changes, storage decision and a private verified food-only photograph location or pending status. A photo alone does not prove the process. No generated picture is pupil evidence.
photo_policy: An adult may use an approved device after food handling has stopped. Photograph only the pupil’s actual food on a plain surface. Keep all people, faces, hands, names, labels, screens and reflections out of the frame. No automatic upload or public posting. Verify a copy with location and other identifying metadata removed before attaching it to private evidence. Keep the device away from food preparation. Restore hand hygiene if returning to food. If a suitable device or checks are unavailable, leave photo status pending and use a truthful written or drawn plate record. Never use the generated recipe pictures as pupil evidence.
no_kitchen: Use the same planned cold wrap with adult-supplied washed, pre-cut vegetables and cooked ready-to-eat beans. Pupils mash, mix, fill and fold using a fork, bowl and clean work surface. No heat or knife is needed. Staff must still approve handwashing with potable water, cleaning, food-safe preparation, labels, allergy controls, supervision and verified cold storage. A checked insulated cold container may be used only if it holds food at 0–5°C. If any requirement cannot be met, use the materials-free simulation and keep practical competence pending.
materials_free: With no safe food facilities, food or equipment, rehearse with empty hands or pictures. The pupil explains or directs the three steps and names a safety action at each point. Record this as planning or simulation, not preparation. Mark the practical and any plate photo pending. Rebook the practical when the adult can meet all safety requirements.
source_basis: Original generic teaching wording checked against current public cleaning, chilling, cross-contamination, food allergy, school allergy and health guidance on 30 October 2026. No external pages, addresses, copied text or named suppliers are included.

assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original three-panel food preparation picture strip for a secondary school recipe card. Landscape 3:1 canvas, three equally sized panels in one horizontal row, separated by clear white gutters. Crisp realistic food illustration, overhead view on a plain clean light surface, suitable for ages 14–16. Panel one: a neat small bowl of washed grated carrot and finely sliced cabbage, with a washed small apple beside it; absolutely no knife, grater, can, packaging, labels or hands. Panel two: a clean mixing bowl showing mashed pale cooked beans mixed with grated carrot, shredded cabbage and a small amount of plain yoghurt, a fork resting safely inside the bowl; show the food as mixed, not whole dry beans. Panel three: a plain white plate with a folded wholemeal wrap filled with the same bean and vegetable mix, the washed apple alongside and a small plain bowl of yoghurt next to the plate. Generic invented ingredients and serving only. Keep each panel simple, spacious, visually distinct, with no background kitchen details. Constraints: no people, hands, faces, body parts, logos, brands, words, letters, numbers, watermarks, decorative icons, raw animal food, dry beans, packaging, utensils in the final serving. Pictures illustrate stages only; do not imply pupil-made evidence. Final image should have a white opaque background.
